subject: MSA & Order Form - productization / output ownership clarifications
messages:
From: Sarah Klein <sarah.klein@helioanalytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@helioanalytics.com, Gabe Moreno <gabe.moreno@clientco.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redlines: MSA & Order Form — IP and productization

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal pushed back on two items in the MSA/Order Form that are blockers for our procurement team: output ownership and any broad training/use license for our data. High level asks from Helio:

- We retain ownership of all output produced by the service (customer output).
- Any training or model improvement using Helio data must be opt-in and scoped (no transfer to third parties).
- Feedback license: Helio will provide limited feedback; any use of that feedback for productization must be non-identifying and not enable resale of Helio-derived models.

I attached our redlines (Helio_MSA_redlines_v1.docx). For speed, can you confirm whether Redwood can accept: (a) customer ownership of outputs, and (b) a narrowly scoped, non-exclusive feedback license limited to internal model improvement (with an explicit prohibition on training external third-party models)?

We'd like to get this over the line this month — procurement has a sprint on the vendor selection.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Klein
Head of Legal Ops, Helio Analytics

Attachment: Helio_MSA_redlines_v1.docx (redline of MSA + Order Form)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Klein <sarah.klein@helioanalytics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA & Order Form — IP and productization

Hi Sarah — appreciate the clear list. Looping in Laura (legal) and Ben (sales/ops) so we can respond with concrete language. Short answers first:

- Customer ownership of outputs: we can accept that the customer holds title to outputs they submit/receive.
- Training/use: Redwood needs a limited license to use de-identified telemetry and aggregated feedback to improve the hosted service. We cannot accept a blanket prohibition on any training that would cover our internal model tuning for latency/quality unless there's an explicit carveout describing scope and safeguards.

Proposed approach from Redwood:
1) Output ownership: Affirmative clause that Helio retains title to Customer Output. Redwood will require a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to the Customer Output solely to provide the service and to improve the service internally (see 2).
2) Productization / feedback license: A narrow feedback/derivative-use license that allows Redwood to use aggregated, de-identified feedback and performance telemetry to improve models and the service UX. This license will expressly prohibit using Helio-owned datasets to train or fine-tune third-party models or for resale.
3) Training opt-in: For any training that uses Helio raw data (PII or proprietary datasets), Redwood will only proceed with explicit, signed opt-in via Order Form addendum.

Laura and Ben — can you review and suggest redline wording? I put a short response document together (Redwood_response_redline_v1.docx) that tracks the above; attaching.

If Helio can accept the above high-level constraints, we can finalize language and move to countersign by next week.

— Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_response_redline_v1.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA & Order Form — IP and productization

Vanessa / Laura — quick suggested language and implementation notes from GTM/ops perspective:

Suggested clause snippet (for the Order Form):
"Customer retains title to all Customer Output. Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, worldwide license to use Customer Output and aggregated telemetry solely to operate the Service and to internally improve its performance and features. Such internal improvements shall not be used to create, train, or otherwise build models or products that are sold or licensed to third parties that are targeted to reproduce Customer Output. Any use of raw Customer Data for model training requires explicit opt-in described in the Order Form."

Implementation guardrails to add to the Contract & SOW:
- Data handling: telemetry and logs used for product improvement will be de-identified/hashed and kept for no longer than 90 days (30 days preferred for sensitive customers).
- Productization carveout: internal use to build features in Redwood's hosted offering is allowed; redistribution or sale of a derivative that reproduces Helio content is prohibited.
- Auditability: Helio can request an incident report if they suspect their data was used inappropriately; Redwood will provide timeline and remediation.

Also flag: if Helio insists on 0% training of any form, we must treat them as "training-opt-out" and that affects model selection and price (we may need to pin to smaller models or Dedicated-only deployment). Recommend we present the legal language plus an ops impact note in one packet.

— Ben

From: Sarah Klein <sarah.klein@helioanalytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Gabe Moreno <gabe.moreno@clientco.com>, legal@helioanalytics.com
Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA & Order Form — IP and productization

Vanessa / Laura / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed language. After an internal review Helio can accept the limited license for aggregated, de-identified telemetry and a productization carveout that is: (1) limited to improving Redwood's hosted service, (2) expressly prohibits resale or creating a Helio-targeted product, and (3) requires signed opt-in for any use of raw Helio data for training.

We've applied a few small edits in our final redline (attached Helio_MSA_redlines_final.docx) to tighten the definition of "de-identified" and to set a 60-day max retention for telemetry used in product improvement for our deal. Helio can't accept a 90-day default but will accept 30 days for the most sensitive datasets if we can add a clause that allows us to change retention via Order Form.

If Redwood accepts the 60-day retention and the explicit opt-in for raw-data training, Helio is ready to proceed to countersign. I've included a DocuSign link for the final MSA/Order Form: https://docusign.com/embedded/ABC123-helio-msafinal

Please confirm and we will route to procurement.

Best,
Sarah
Head of Legal Ops, Helio Analytics

Attachment: Helio_MSA_redlines_final.docx
